rationale: The admitted v2 makes a structural, not editorial, change. Research shows that a Data Act mandate is non-exclusive, OEM-specific access costs and portal substitutes persist, and a neutral-intermediary role can conflict with proprietary analytics (r08-dga-structure-fork, r11-oem-api-cost-and-contract, r12-oem-platform-substitute, r13-legal-agency-not-exclusive, r20-mechanism-ownership-fork). The redesign therefore narrows the customer, problem, payer, offer, distribution, and compounding mechanism to one founder-accessible installer, one commercial-solar inverter family, and one recurring dispatch-triage decision. It uses documented Fronius local access as the first obtainability test and treats Data Act requests as fallback rather than the moat (r10-fronius-access-test, r22-obtainability-is-oem-specific). It shifts economics from low per-device fees, savings share, and heterogeneous connector work to an OEM-family onboarding fee plus an annual per-site installer contract, with explicit access-cost, contribution-margin, three-times-value, label-return, and renewal gates because willingness to pay, CAC, margins, and repeat use remain unproven (r15-wtp-renewal-cac-unproven, r16-unit-economics-unproven, r17-repeat-use-unproven). Finally, it places the proposed control point in the installer's maintenance workflow and technician close-out records, directly addressing the scarce-label cold start (r18-fault-label-cold-start, r19-outcome-label-dependency), while honestly preserving the unsigned installer agreement, owner permissions, legal classification, and field sufficiency as critical dependencies rather than invented evidence.
